Pointwise intervals for fixed facet estimates and contrasts

Source: R/api-facet-intervals.R, R/api-plotting-facet-intervals.R
mfrm_facet_intervals.Rd

Quantify uncertainty in fixed non-Person facet locations, two-way interaction cells, or prespecified linear contrasts from a supported fit_mfrm() result. Inspect Estimate, Status, CIEligible, CoverageQualified, and InferenceReview together in summary(intervals): missing bounds do not imply zero uncertainty, and Status = "fixed" marks constraint-pinned targets without inferential intervals.

Usage

mfrm_facet_intervals(
  fit,
  facet = NULL,
  contrasts = NULL,
  method = c("model", "sandwich", "profile"),
  clusters = NULL,
  adjust = FALSE,
  level = 0.95,
  scale = c("native", "standardized"),
  comparison_review = NULL,
  anchor_covariance = NULL,
  independent_anchors = FALSE,
  interaction = NULL,
  profile_control = list()
)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_facet_intervals'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_facet_intervals'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_facet_intervals'
confint(object, parm = NULL, level = object$settings$level, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_facet_intervals'
vcov(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_facet_intervals'
plot(
  x,
  comparison = TRUE,
  draw = TRUE,
  preset = "standard",
  title = paste(x$settings$facet, if (identical(x$settings$target,
    "category_step_offsets")) "step offsets" else "estimates and contrasts"),
  subtitle = paste0(format(100 * x$settings$level, trim = TRUE), if
    (identical(x$settings$method, "profile")) "% connected profile interval | " else
    "% pointwise normal intervals | ", if (identical(x$settings$method, "profile"))
    "Profile likelihood" else if (x$settings$method == "sandwich") paste0("Sandwich | ",
    x$settings$clusters, " independent clusters assumed") else if
(identical(x$settings$procedure, "cml_conditional_information"))
    "Conditional information" else if (identical(x$settings$uncertainty,
    "independent_anchor_delta")) "Information + anchor source" else
    "Observed information"),
  caption = if (any(!is.finite(x$table$Estimate)))
    paste0("Not estimated: no point or interval | ",
    "Crosses: estimated points with unavailable intervals") else if (any(x$table$Status
    != "available"))
    "Open diamonds: fixed targets | Crosses: unavailable selected intervals" else NULL,
  reference = 0,
  show_legend = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

fit

Supported fit_mfrm() result (ordinary or estimated-population RSM/PCM MML, one- or two-family GPCM MML, or native full/comparison-only RSM/PCM CML; JML structural intervals are unsupported).

facet

Non-Person facet name (e.g., "Rater"); omit when selecting interaction, comparison_review, or a CML comparison-only fit.

contrasts

Optional named numeric matrix with columns matching all levels of facet (or all interaction Target cells).

method

"model" (default: inverse full joint observed marginal or conditional information), "sandwich" (independent-Person or cluster marginal-score sandwich H^{-1} (sum_g s_g s_g') H^{-1} for ordinary fixed-\(N(0,1)\) RSM/PCM MML), or experimental "profile" (reoptimizes one pairwise +1/-1 contrast over residual variance >= 0 in unanchored estimated-normal direct RSM/PCM MML).

clusters

Optional one-row-per-Person data.frame (Person, Cluster) and G/(G - 1) finite-cluster multiplier (FALSE default) for method = "sandwich".

adjust

Optional one-row-per-Person data.frame (Person, Cluster) and G/(G - 1) finite-cluster multiplier (FALSE default) for method = "sandwich".

level

Pointwise confidence level in (0, 1) (default 0.95).

scale

"native" (default logit ability units) or "standardized" (divides zero-sum contrasts or comparison_review interaction contrasts by the same fit's population SD \(\sigma\) under method = "model" and fixed-\(N(0,1)\) or intercept-only normal MML).

comparison_review

Optional describe_mfrm_data() review supplying identifiable facet-by-origin interaction contrasts in full RSM/PCM MML.

anchor_covariance

Optional full source-anchor sampling covariance matrix (matching all direct anchors on the noncentered facet) and explicit independent-sample declaration (FALSE default) for direct intercept-only RSM/PCM anchor-origin MML.

independent_anchors

Optional full source-anchor sampling covariance matrix (matching all direct anchors on the noncentered facet) and explicit independent-sample declaration (FALSE default) for direct intercept-only RSM/PCM anchor-origin MML.

interaction

Optional fitted two-way interaction name (e.g., "Rater:Criterion") in full single-interaction RSM/PCM MML (method = "model", scale = "native").

profile_control

Named list for method = "profile": quad_points (default 81) and max_quad_points (321), checked against 2*q - 1.

x

Output from mfrm_facet_intervals() or two-family confint(fit, parm = "steps"). The latter displays within-level step offsets. See confint.mfrm_fit() for the target and qualification.

Also for print(): An object returned by mfrm_facet_intervals().

...

For print.mfrm_facet_intervals(): Unused by print and summary methods.

For plot(): Unused.

object

An object returned by mfrm_facet_intervals() or two-family confint(fit, parm = "steps").

parm

For confint(), optional distinct target names from object$table$Target. Extracts the stored limits without recalculation; level must match the saved level. Use mfrm_facet_intervals() to calculate a different level, or confint(fit, parm = "steps") for step offsets. Unavailable limits remain NA; inspect summary(object) for their eligibility and reasons.

comparison

Logical. With a sandwich result, also show its ordinary model-based interval. With source-propagated anchors, show the separate conditional-on-anchors interval. Both use the same point estimate.

draw

Logical; FALSE returns exact plotted data without opening a device.

preset

A package plot preset, for example "standard" or "monochrome".

title

Optional returned text; NULL omits it. Defaults describe the facet, exact confidence level, method and fixed/unavailable symbols. This text is not drawn; use plot_data(p, "notes") and plot_data(p, "title") to retrieve it.

subtitle

Optional returned text; NULL omits it. Defaults describe the facet, exact confidence level, method and fixed/unavailable symbols. This text is not drawn; use plot_data(p, "notes") and plot_data(p, "title") to retrieve it.

caption

Optional returned text; NULL omits it. Defaults describe the facet, exact confidence level, method and fixed/unavailable symbols. This text is not drawn; use plot_data(p, "notes") and plot_data(p, "title") to retrieve it.

reference

Optional finite vertical reference; default zero. Use NULL to omit it. This is not a rater-quality threshold.

show_legend

Logical; show the method legend (default TRUE).

Value

An mfrm_facet_intervals object (summary(), plot(), vcov(), apa_table()) with table, covariance/model_covariance, parameter_covariance, person_scores/cluster_scores (sandwich), anchor_uncertainty (when supplied), profile/profile_attempts (profile), checks, numerical_checks, and settings.

For plot(): Invisibly, a ggplot object; plot_data() retains the table, contrast coefficients, settings and labels, and as_ggplot() remains idempotent on the returned object.

Details

Covariance propagation and constraints. For constrained locations \(b = b_0 + J\eta\) and contrast matrix \(C\), target covariance is \(C J V_\eta J^\top C^\top\), where \(V_\eta\) is extracted after inverting the full joint information across all free structural, step, interaction, slope, and population coordinates (Status = "information_unavailable" if singular; Status = "insufficient_cluster_rank" withholds sandwich bounds while retaining Model* columns).

Standardized contrasts. With scale = "standardized", native contrast \(d\) and log-variance \(\lambda = \log(\sigma^2)\) define \(t = d/\sigma\) with full delta-method variance: $$\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\widehat t) = \frac{\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\widehat d) + \widehat d^2\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\widehat\lambda)/4 - \widehat d\,\widehat{\mathrm{Cov}}(\widehat d,\widehat\lambda)} {\widehat\sigma^2}.$$

Anchor-source propagation. With anchor_covariance and independent_anchors = TRUE, implicit differentiation \(S = -H_{uu}^{-1}H_{ua}\) yields source derivative \(D = t_u S + t_a\) and total covariance \(t_u V_{\mathrm{cond}} t_u^\top + D V_{\mathrm{anchor}} D^\top\), retaining conditional bounds in Conditional* and reusable by mfrm_population_intervals().

CML and profile contrasts. Full CML uses unregularized inverse conditional information (scale = "native"); comparison-only CML reuses saved subspace covariances without refitting. Profile contrasts report ProfileEstimate alongside SourceEstimate without Wald SE/vcov(). Worked examples and bounded coverage evaluations appear on the package website (https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/mfrmr/articles/mfrmr-facet-intervals.html).

plot() method: Plot fixed-facet interval methods

For plot(): Fixed targets use open diamonds without inferential intervals. A conditionally fixed anchor can have a source-propagated interval; the comparison displays its conditional fixed value separately. Method labels distinguish source propagation from conditional observed information. Unavailable intervals in either displayed method use crosses; an ordinary comparison interval does not substitute for a missing sandwich interval. The zero line is a reference, not a threshold of practical importance or a rater-quality rule. No fit or covariance is recalculated. Target order is preserved. Weak-information cautions remain in the returned data and appear in the default subtitle. Custom or omitted subtitles change display only. For experimental two-family GPCM locations, the axis uses fixed-N(0,1) ability units and the default subtitle states the location reference and the lack of established coverage, with a deficient Person-score rank caution when applicable. These are not uniform expected-rating differences. Standardized contrast axes use population SD units; returned notes identify whether SD uncertainty is estimated or the known SD is one. Reviewed interaction contrasts retain group direction, panel weights and scale in their source result; returned labels distinguish them from facet locations. Native CML intervals are labeled conditional information. Their returned notes describe asymptotic validity without implying weak information or an estimated ability population SD. When a comparison has no estimate, its row is labeled "not estimated" and has no point or interval. An empty display range is only an axis placeholder; it does not assign a value to unavailable targets. Joint interaction-cell results retain cell identities, counts and sparse flags in plot_data(p, "interaction_cells"). Their axis uses additive predictor shifts; row labels show the two level names in fitted facet order. Units follow the fixed N(0,1) ability scale. Positive effects raise expected coded scores relative to the jointly fitted main effects. These pointwise intervals are not fixed-baseline bias screens or fairness labels.

Session plot defaults

See mfrmr_visual_diagnostics for options(mfrmr.plot_preset), argument precedence, and appearance when saving or reusing a plot.

  • Zeileis, A., Koell, S., & Graham, N. (2020). Journal of Statistical Software, 95(1), 1–36. doi:10.18637/jss.v095.i01 .

Examples

# Long-running workflow; run explicitly when needed.
# example("mfrm_facet_intervals", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
ratings <- load_mfrmr_data("example_core")
fit <- fit_mfrm(ratings, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",
  model = "RSM", method = "MML", rating_min = 1, rating_max = 4,
  category_policy = "preserve")
intervals <- mfrm_facet_intervals(fit, "Rater", method = "sandwich")
summary(intervals)[, c("Target", "Estimate", "SE", "Lower", "Upper",
  "Status", "CIEligible", "InferenceReview")]
# Keep all rows: a missing interval does not imply a missing point.
plot(intervals) # Crosses mark retained estimates with unavailable intervals.

# Compare two selected raters, rather than each rater against the origin.
# Here choose the first two example labels; prespecify your own comparison.
raters <- unique(as.character(ratings$Rater))
contrast <- matrix(0, 1, length(raters), dimnames = list(
  paste(raters[1], "minus", raters[2]), raters))
contrast[1, 1:2] <- c(1, -1)
difference <- mfrm_facet_intervals(fit, "Rater", contrasts = contrast)
summary(difference)[, c("Target", "Estimate", "SE", "Lower", "Upper", "Status")]
# With the default negative rater sign, a positive contrast means the first
# rater is more severe. Units are native logits. An interval containing zero
# leaves the direction uncertain; it does not establish equivalence.

# Estimate the population SD in this same model before standardizing.
# Even an intercept-only population model needs one row per person.
persons <- unique(ratings["Person"])
population_fit <- fit_mfrm(ratings, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"),
  "Score", model = "RSM", method = "MML", population_formula = ~ 1,
  person_data = persons, person_id = "Person",
  rating_min = 1, rating_max = 4, category_policy = "preserve", quad_points = 61)
standardized <- mfrm_facet_intervals(population_fit, "Rater",
  contrasts = contrast, scale = "standardized")
summary(standardized)
# Estimate is now in fitted ability-population SD units; its delta-method
# interval includes uncertainty in that SD. It is not a Wald z statistic.

# CML estimates the native contrast without an ability distribution.
if (requireNamespace("lpSolve", quietly = TRUE)) {
  cml_fit <- fit_mfrm(ratings, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",
    model = "RSM", method = "CML", rating_min = 1, rating_max = 4,
    category_policy = "preserve")
  cml_ci <- mfrm_facet_intervals(cml_fit, "Rater", contrasts = contrast)
  summary(cml_ci)
  apa_table(cml_ci)
  file <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds") # Choose a lasting path for your analysis
  saveRDS(cml_ci, file)
  saved <- readRDS(file)
  summary(saved) # Same conditional-information result, without refitting
  # Use plot(saved) for a figure; ordinary mfrm_results() does not accept CML.
}
} # }
